# Common Conformance Questions

A discriminator is a case that separates a correct candidate from a defective one. The [member-conformance](#member-conformance), [universal-construction](#universal-construction-discriminators) and [assurance](#assurance-discriminators) tables supply acceptance criterion 5 of the [C3 Construction Contract](../PRODUCT.md#c3-construction-contract), within the member's applicable scope. Construction and integrated-closure checks have their own section and are evaluated at those decisions.

Both tenants are evaluated against the same independently specified expectations. The reviewer takes in these expectations and the actual source before inspecting the candidate, states applicable obligations and reports uncovered scope. No passing result is recorded here. Evidence binding follows the [frame requirement](../requirements/README.md#bounded-transitions-and-reference-frames); reduction and interpretation coverage follow their common requirement owners.

The candidate's admitted common input fixes its discriminator set under [Candidate Comparison](../PRODUCT.md#candidate-comparison). A later revision does not change an earlier assessment's basis. Unmatched scope remains explicit until the candidates bind the same ratified comparison input.

## Member Conformance

Apply each case to the member's owned determinations and affected consumer bindings. Record applicability under [Construction Authority](../PRODUCT.md#construction-authority). A local review accounts for its scope; integrated assessment covers cross-member coverage and comparisons. An absent integrated assessment does not by itself fail a member's local criterion 5.

| Discriminator | Expected distinction |
|---|---|
| A derivation or independence argument is claimed | Each claimed derivation shows its premises. Claimed independence is argued, not assumed. |
| A family argument accounts for edited rules but omits inherited deciding rules or their consumers | Coverage includes the material rules and actual consumers in the declared family, or a supported account that no separate consumer applies. A blank field, generic referral, coarser grouping or whole-member preamble cannot supply a missing relation. |
| A new foundations introduction accompanies unchanged rival rules in the consumers | Correspondence alone does not establish reduction. The deciding consumers must use one shared determination or a justified refinement. |
| A candidate is shorter but ordinary entry still requires the same independent reconciliations | Compare the actual deciding paths and acquisition against the exact predecessor and preceding tenant candidate. A smaller body alone is not a positive reduction witness. |
| A candidate unifies a recurring rule and retains a necessary domain exception | Establish actual shared-law use, preserved outcomes and the exception's owner. Reduction can hold without a universal percentage or word-count decrease. |
| Outcome-driven development is presented only as a vocabulary for operations | Show how generic outcome-driven transition contracts govern construction, evaluation, continuation, recovery and termination, with independently specified cases and justified additional policies. These generic obligations do not require adoption of the optional typed-graph profile. |
| Several predecessor clauses are implemented by one shared successor law | Evaluate each material obligation and its consuming bindings. Shared ownership can conserve several claims without retaining their former document partitions; a bare link cannot supply omitted meaning. |
| A candidate deletes an exception to make the core smaller | Size reduction cannot erase a material obligation. Give it a valid disposition and preserve its required behavior, or obtain the owning removal decision. |
| A domain rule is replaced by a shared-law reference | Preserve its material trigger, modal force, adoption conditions and exceptions. The shared owner and domain binding must supply the determination without circular referral. |
| A required generic rule is owned only by an optional profile | Generic use can obtain that determination without adopting the profile; profile-specific additions retain their selection boundary. |
| A functional helper is promoted into a new public mechanism | Require the material distinction or independent boundary that needs it. Shared machinery and subordinate helpers do not create new semantic or authority owners by naming alone. |
| A bounded object is declared a Markov object because its interface is small | An ordinary useful boundary supplies no proof of the stronger sufficiency or independence claim. State its assumptions and evidence; an unsupported claim stays unresolved. |
| An a_c model omits a source condition but passes its schema check | The model fails fidelity for a decision affected by that condition. Mechanical validity cannot authorise the work that the owning source prohibits. |
| A faithful a_c fragment is offered as the whole method's interpretation | Account for every material owned determination and required dependency. The fragment establishes only its covered scope; missing material coverage prevents C3 closure for that tenant. |
| A frame uses an a_c projection rather than copying a clause verbatim | Assess fidelity and task sufficiency against the owning source. Different encoding alone is no defect; changed obligations or permissions are. |
| A compressed constraint surface treats an unresolved premise as unrestricted freedom | Preserve the unresolved dependency and apply the relevant stop, acquisition or refinement rule. Unknown permission is not a grant. |
| A task has several solutions inside the same constraint surface | Permit the alternatives that satisfy its contract. The method constrains admissibility without absorbing the worker's internal solution strategy. |
| A projection changes “not required” into “prohibited”, or preference into obligation | The changed permitted work is a fidelity defect unless an authorised successor relation establishes the change. Matching digests or valid schema do not repair it. |
| Ordinary entry points to an earlier return or interpretation marked current, or an internal check passes while its published acquisition route fails | Bind the current source, signature, program, maps, instructions and evidence boundary; reproduce the offered route. Earlier artifacts retain historical standing. Refusing stale inputs contains the failure but does not establish a usable current publication or semantic coverage. |
| Information and its representation differ | Agreement in structure cannot establish identical meaning or semantic fidelity. |
| Identity is unchanged while content changes | The current state, and whether an earlier observation still applies, are considered separately. |
| Typed producers and consumers disagree | The incompatible domain or precondition is made explicit. Fields of the same shape do not make a valid join. |
| Assessment A failed and required coverage B is uncovered | A's authenticated failure and its citations survive, and B stays unresolved. Every planned assessment's returned judgement is authenticated against its producer, subject, basis and supporting evidence. B is required coverage outside those assessments, not an omitted planned judgement. |
| A genuinely planned assessment carries a judgement from a different subject | Plan membership does not authenticate the returned judgement. The misbound result cannot satisfy the assessment obligation. |
| The context a task needs is interdependent and does not fit one actor | Narrowing the task lawfully, handing it to another capable actor, or a truthful stop keeps the material obligations. |
| A frame fits its byte limit but irrelevant material obscures a required dependency | Size alone does not establish adequacy. Keep the material dependency, exclude irrelevant material and evaluate actual use under the [frame requirement](../requirements/README.md#bounded-transitions-and-reference-frames). |
| A frame or task changes after its trial, or actor instructions supply the expected answer | Bind the actual tested packet and independently specified expectations. Report the narrower evidence; a rewritten trial or matching source pin does not establish current task sufficiency. |
| An author opens a fresh context to review its own candidate | A new context does not establish independent authorship or supply missing review authority. Ported contributions retain their authorship; the contributor's review cannot supply independent acceptance of them. Relevant common sources may still be shared by an independent reviewer. |
| A coordination frame omits frontier items from its current attention | Excluded work remains open; a bounded view cannot silently dispose it. The next decision retains its material dependencies. |
| A new observation exposes more obligations, or a destination is revised to make the current candidate pass | Discovery may increase the frontier while improving knowledge. Counts alone do not measure progress. A revised destination requires its owning decision and cannot establish that the original destination was reached. |
| One directly authorised task fits a sufficient frame | The generic method permits the direct activation, subject to any separately required assessment. It imposes no fixed role inventory or actor sequence. |
| A peer configuration has no central Executive, or a task uses responsibilities outside the familiar three roles | Evaluate the configuration against the task, dependencies, actor limits, authority and required assurance. Different labels or topology neither reject nor accept it. The installed configuration selected to build this release retains its own scope. |
| Actors redistribute work during execution, including work with effects of uncertain completion | The permitted reconfiguration retains outstanding obligations and result dependencies, resolves material effect uncertainty before dependent action, and preserves authority and required independence. Self-organisation supplies no exemption from these conditions. |
| An arrangement is called optimal because it is familiar, persistent or self-organised | Adequacy and optimality remain separate claims. An optimality claim needs stated objectives, constraints and comparison scope with supporting evidence. Different models or objectives can favour different configurations. |
| A coordinator receives a compact task result that omits a blocker material to delivery | Small size is insufficient. The coordinator retains the longer-term outcome and acquires the information needed for the next decision through its permitted frame inputs. Missing information cannot be assumed favourable. |
| A material dependency changes or a new observation invalidates an earlier claim | Affected applicability and validity are checked before reuse, including when the candidate's bytes are unchanged. Demonstrably independent supported work is kept. |
| A task packet contains relevant rules but lacks material context or authority | A rule packet alone is insufficient. The activated frame binds the contract, subject, evidence, capability and permitted effects required for the task. |
| A fresh actor has no private history, and a retained summary disagrees with the current workspace | Acquire the current subject and its authoritative inputs, correct the stale account, retain applicable work and continue within the grant. Discarding context does not erase the workspace or prove an uncertain external effect absent. |
| An interruption leaves work partly written | Recovery uses the current workspace and the applicable work state. It does not erase progress or invent a completed assessment. |
| A parse or map succeeds | The claim stays mechanical until independently sufficient semantic and practical evidence exists. |
| A change to work carriers or process is proposed as new law | The claimed obligation is justified by its purpose and material relation, or identified as unsupported overhead. |
| The same requirements are realised by software, a human team or a mixed process | Each tenant supplies its computational calculus, concrete execution binding and conformance evidence. Common requirements decide fitness; the kind of executor alone neither rejects nor accepts the realisation. Generic procedures preserve those permitted choices, including an adequate human process using current records and direct observation without code or complete event-history replay ([binding requirement](../requirements/README.md#build-tenant-binding-requirement)). |
| A faster execution plan merges two required independent assessments or substitutes an automated result for a required human decision | Matching outputs or lower cost cannot discharge the lost independence or authority obligation. The binding fails conformance. |
| Two environments use one computational calculus, or one actor performs different kinds of operation | Each binding must satisfy the calculus's laws. Different stacks do not force duplicate calculi; actor identity does not determine operation kind or grant authority. |
| An a_c model of a human process passes structural validation | The representation neither selects an automated executor nor establishes that the human process meets its requirements. Execution conformance needs its own applicable evidence. |
| Two loci in one candidate decide the same question | One is the [owning locus](../requirements/README.md#single-ownership-requirement). The other refers to it, or refines it with a mapping back to it. A frame's copy names its owner. No rule of precedence between loci substitutes for an owner. |
| A member or profile defines its own result values | Its owner maps each value, with its declared predicate and meaning-determining conditions, to exactly one core result. Failure, undecidability, non-performance and unknown effect completion never map to a higher standing. The predicate and domain outcome travel with the core value ([requirement](../requirements/README.md#single-result-algebra-requirement)). |
| A lifecycle label or classification is used to decide admission, compliance or closure | Recorded data and the evaluation or authorised decision remain distinct. The actual determination uses the core result contract; calling it data cannot exempt it, and a core referral cannot replace a missing domain map. |
| A conserved heading now carries a different obligation, or a superseded row names only the old section | Compare the required and permitted decisions on the same material case, including modal force, triggers, scope and exceptions, under the [disposition requirement](../requirements/README.md#successor-disposition-requirement). An indicative rewrite is judged by its meaning, not its grammatical form. Each superseded claim identifies its replacement relation and owning loci; a proposed relation remains pending until accepted. |
| A frame's task returns a result | The frame carries the core result algebra or its profile's mapping into it. |
| A functor or categorical join is claimed | Before the claim, objects, arrows, arrow equality, identity and composition are given and the functor laws are shown. Otherwise the claim is a hypothesis ([standard](../requirements/README.md#categorical-demonstration-standard)). |
| A rewrite or refinement step is applied | The law that permits it is declared for the subject. An exact step preserves meaning. An approximate step states its adequacy relation and an end-to-end bound. |

## Universal Construction Discriminators

These cases test the candidate's deciding rules under the [construction requirement](../requirements/README.md#universal-construction-requirement). They apply to member criterion 5 within the member's declared responsibility; the integrated checks below evaluate their composition and actual use.

| Discriminator | Expected distinction |
|---|---|
| Internal tasks pass while a required end-to-end feature fails | Keep the outer failure and diagnose the affected join; local completion does not establish Z. |
| Every selected operation is lawful but the result fails the chosen outcome constraints | Preserve the distinction between admissible construction and delivered outcome. The specification supplies Z; a calculus or lawful execution supplies no automatic satisfaction or acceptance. |
| A report called a bug could concern implementation, requirements or missing observations | Apply one intake and causal diagnosis. Correct the supported affected relation, or acquire evidence and retain unresolved alternatives. The label supplies no repair class or permission. |
| A requirement is weakened until the current realisation passes | A change to Z needs its owning decision and downstream re-entry. It neither proves the former Z nor erases the original counterexample. |
| A predictive model agrees with observations while the required outcome is absent, or predicts incorrectly while the outcome holds | Prediction accuracy and satisfaction of the normative specification are different claims. Diagnose each against its own predicate and support; neither conclusion determines the other. |
| A strategy is selected solely by its name, or a cheaper plan loses required assurance | Select within the outcome constraints, using material resource, risk and feedback tradeoffs. Cost savings supply no waiver. Preserve incomparable alternatives and unsupported estimates explicitly. |
| Every recursive step preserves an invariant but the process does not deliver | Preservation alone proves no progress or termination. State the actual support for continuing or the unresolved stop; no generic termination proof is required merely to perform bounded work. |
| A limit is exhausted, an observation exposes more work, or an ongoing maintenance loop continues | Distinguish attempt termination, useful discovery, continuing maintenance and delivered outcome. Neither elapsed work nor a changed count supplies the conclusion by itself. |
| A restart or later disturbance contradicts a cached successful result | Reacquire the bound current subject, reopen affected claims and preserve independently applicable work. Resolve uncertain effects sufficiently before a dependent action. |

## Assurance Discriminators

These cases assess the member text under criterion 5 and the [assurance requirement](../requirements/ASSURANCE.md). Actual operation of the affected paths is assessed at the integrated boundary below. One bounded demonstration may cover several cases; table rows impose no separate-run quota.

| Counterexample or adequate case | Required distinction |
|---|---|
| Every local check passes, but a postcondition does not establish the next precondition or the final property does not imply Z | The member requires the missing preservation or coverage argument and withholds the unsupported end-to-end conclusion. It retains supported local results. |
| A histogram has the right keys but incorrect counts; a key-only test passes | The check establishes only its target predicate. Assertion provenance identifies whether that predicate is a necessary condition or is sufficient for the claimed requirement. A faithful count assertion detects the count defect within its scope. |
| Two admissible states have identical acquired observations but opposite truth values for the asserted obligation | The checker cannot claim a sound complete decision from those observations. It acquires distinguishing evidence, justifies a narrower scope or returns an indeterminate judgment. Unavailable observation and not-performed evaluation retain their distinct meanings. |
| A test copies its expected answer from the implementation and cites the requirement's digest | Execution provenance and text identity do not establish assertion fidelity or an independent upstream derivation. A supported local regression claim remains usable. |
| A human or probabilistic checker can soundly return satisfied or indeterminate on the same observations | The model admits both outcomes. A universal soundness claim covers every admitted conclusion; a selected deterministic model retains its scope, and a probability claim needs its own distribution and evidence. |
| Two implementations or reviewers agree through the same wrong interpretation, fixture or received contribution | Agreement is not counted as independent evidence merely because actors differ. Shared causes and port authorship remain visible; validation of the common expectation uses its separate purpose and evidence. |
| Miss rates are multiplied without conditional independence, or an injected-defect score is reported as whole-product correctness probability | The numerical claim requires its model, justified dependence and calibration scope. Unsupported quantification stays unresolved while bounded observations retain their standing. |
| Finite successful examples or a schema-valid formula are called a proof of a universal preservation law | The formal obligation, its discharged argument, structural checking and bounded execution evidence retain distinct scopes. Bounded work can proceed where its governing conditions permit it. |
| A governing requirement changes but expected answers and acceptance evidence are silently retained | Affected assertions and applicability are reassessed through the owning change authority. The original evidence and counterexample retain their subjects. |
| An implementation or environment dependency changes but the only selection relation is requirement-to-test provenance | Impact includes material execution and validity dependencies. Missing influence information cannot justify exclusion; new uncovered obligations generate work and mandatory gates remain applicable. |
| A local repair has supported isolation from an unchanged obligation and its evidence conditions | The applicable unchanged evidence may be retained alongside reassessment of affected claims. The method does not demand full re-execution solely because the subject has changed. |
| Selection is cheap but omits a material obligation, or selection overhead exceeds the saved execution | The plan accounts for required assurance, residual uncertainty and total relevant cost. Broader execution is available; cheap selection or a fixed full-suite habit is not evidence of adequacy or efficiency. |

## Construction And Integrated Closure

Applicable integrated evidence follows [Assurance of Construction](../requirements/ASSURANCE.md): the expected conclusions have assertion provenance, the runs have execution provenance, and retained evidence has supported applicability. These conditions use the existing criteria and carriers.

These checks evaluate the recorded construction decisions and integrated candidate under the installed builder. They do not add candidate-text predicates to member criterion 5. The Executive applies the acceptance checks; the integrated Reviewer evaluates the whole-candidate obligations before C3 closure. Head-to-head evaluation follows [Candidate Comparison](../PRODUCT.md#candidate-comparison), with the same tasks, independently specified expectations and acquisition conditions. An unassessed candidate is not evidence that its peer qualifies.

| Discriminator | Expected distinction |
|---|---|
| Each member passes its local checks while two members still decide the same shared question differently | C3 closure requires the integrated reduction assessment. Separate satisfied member results cannot erase the cross-member contradiction. |
| A member reviewer agrees that a proposed replacement is clear, but no owner decision accepts its changed meaning | Review may support the proposal; dependent member acceptance waits for the exact replacement decision recorded in the ticket. A construction grant does not supply that acceptance. |
| Five member criteria are satisfied and the sixth is missing, stale or falsified | The installed conjunction withholds member acceptance and preserves all component results. A general favourable verdict cannot replace missing or adverse evidence. Supported inapplicability of a conditional obligation is recorded separately; it does not waive any of the six criteria. |
| A control actor answers correctly while the candidate's frame causes an incorrect answer | Preserve the applicable required task judgment under criterion 4. Control success neither proves that the fixture supplied the answer nor removes the frame-use failure. Attribution of benefit is a separate claim; an applicability correction needs its own governing reason. |
| Separate members explain construction, triage and recovery but their consumers cannot carry one feature through the composition | Integrated assessment checks the shared owners and actual deciding path from the selected outcome through bounded work, observation, diagnosis and lawful continuation or closure. Criterion 4 evidence exercises the applicable path under independently specified expectations; prose alone does not establish use. Existing applicable evidence can support several cases; no separate run per table row is imposed. |
| Assertion provenance, formal interpretation and execution records exist separately but do not join on the claimed obligation | The affected demonstration follows the source obligation through its interpreted predicate and observed subject to the supported conclusion. It exposes a weak assertion, an insufficient observation and a shared-error case, retaining each claim's bounded standing. |
| A repair invalidates some claims while other evidence remains applicable | The affected actual-use demonstration selects reassessment from supported impact, preserves known failures and unknown coverage, and combines new results with justified reuse. It exercises both valid retention and a missed-dependency or changed-oracle case; complete fresh execution is not required where the governing assurance is already established. |

Logical review is a reviewer's reasoned reading. It finds counterexamples and contradictions without running anything. Actual-use cases do real construction, observe genuine defects, keep the uncertainty of effects, and re-enter the method at the right stage.

The token-transfer test in [A_C_DEPENDENCY](../requirements/A_C_DEPENDENCY.md#proof-claims) tests a_c separately from the method's interpretation fidelity. Source comparison independent of the author, mechanical checks, formal derivations and practical adequacy remain different kinds of evidence.

1	# Assurance Of Construction
2	
3	Source: this Product's [Universal Construction Model](../PRODUCT.md#universal-construction-model).
4	
5	This requirement owns the relationship between construction, assertions, observations and the claims they support. It applies the [universal construction requirement](README.md#universal-construction-requirement) to assurance under finite resources. Foundations own the shared relationships; the Spec Method and profiles bind them to their operations. A tenant chooses their representation and execution within these obligations.
6	
7	## Preservation Through Construction
8	
9	A construction binds its starting state A and required outcome Z under the [universal construction model](../PRODUCT.md#universal-construction-model), with its governing basis and material assumptions, written Γ. The predicate for Z includes required effects and trace properties where these matter. The following notation states proof obligations; writing an implication does not discharge it.
10	
11	For a sequence of transformations, let `X_i` be the state or trace domain at boundary i, `F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1)` the declared transition relation, and `P_i` the property to retain or establish there. A claimed preservation step has the form:
12	
13	```text
14	For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').
15	```
16	
17	The relation accounts for the outcomes, effects and assumptions material to the claim. A relation covering successful completion alone supplies no claim about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects. Handling those cases follows the existing result, authority and recovery contracts. The real execution's conformance to the relation is a separate obligation.
18	
19	An end-to-end preservation argument establishes the initial condition, each step's applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the connection from the final property to Z. In particular, the preceding postcondition must establish the next precondition or the missing condition must be acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination and the availability of a suitable next step.
20	
21	Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or remain unchanged. Changes to the governing outcome or meaning follow its owner and successor rules.
22	
23	The algorithmic account states the required operation, the informational account states the meaning and distinctions retained, and the computational binding states how work and observations are realised. Claims across these accounts identify their maps and preservation obligations. Execution by a person, machine or mixed arrangement does not discharge those obligations by itself. A commuting diagram, functor or equivalence claim requires the [categorical demonstration](README.md#categorical-demonstration-standard) appropriate to it.
24	
25	## Assertions And Observation
26	
27	For a selected source obligation r, let `Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω)` be its required predicate over a declared domain Ω of cases. A case includes the inputs, behaviour and material environment needed for that obligation. The interpretation retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected text; it does not prove this interpretation faithful.
28	
29	An assertion targets a predicate `q_t`. The candidate states whether that predicate is the full obligation or a narrower claim. The two directions have different consequences:
30	
31	```text
32	Q_r implies q_t                : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
33	q_t implies Q_r                : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
34	(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.
35	```
36	
37	These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of passing tests does not supply that argument by its count.
38	
39	Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and `T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R uses the method's [single result algebra](README.md#single-result-algebra-requirement). A deterministic checker is a functional special case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted conclusions, not a favourable selected run. Here, `indeterminate` names the core judgment whose admissible evidence cannot decide the evaluated predicate; it remains distinct from an evaluation that was not performed. A claim or work item can remain unresolved for either reason; unresolved work is not an additional judgment value. In the following obligations, `sat` and `fal` denote the satisfied and falsified judgments about `q_t`, not new execution states:
40	
41	```text
42	For every s in Ω:
43	  (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).
44	  (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).
45	```
46	
47	The candidate identifies what supports each claimed direction and where it is unresolved. A relation admitting both a sound satisfied judgment and an indeterminate judgment need not always decide the case. A restricted deterministic model retains its scope and an actual checker requires its own conformance account. An observed test pass remains an observation when the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not become established satisfaction of the source obligation. The same distinction applies to a reported failure. The observation binding itself needs support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim uses its declared distribution over outcomes and the risk contract below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities.
48	
49	A checker that always decides `q_t` correctly using only π requires:
50	
51	```text
52	For all s, s' in Ω:
53	  π(s) = π(s')  implies  q_t(s) = q_t(s').
54	```
55	
56	This states observation sufficiency. If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between them. Further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations retain their required distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was not performed.
57	
58	## Parallel Derivation And Mutual Assurance
59	
60	Construction and assurance can follow different paths from a common obligation. For `requirement → refinement → realisation`, assertions derived from the requirement check its applicable conditions in the realisation; assertions derived from the refinement check its more detailed obligations there. User-acceptance and build-level tests can instantiate these paths. The roles identify the selected sources and subject in this example; they prescribe no stage names or test classes.
61	
62	The expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies that give it meaning. Execution provenance identifies the actual checker, exact subject and applicable environment, inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they support. Execution logs alone cannot establish that the expected answer follows from the requirement.
63	
64	An implementation-derived test can be useful for regression or a stated local property. Repeating the implementation's decision supplies no independent justification for its fidelity to an upstream obligation. A shorter assertion path can be easier to inspect and execute than construction; that is a supported design claim for the selected path, not a guarantee of correctness, coverage or independence. Valid distinct implementations can produce different outputs within the same acceptable relation; equality of outputs is not always the oracle.
65	
66	Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Assurance accounts for shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations, copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors, model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence. Porting retains authorship and common dependencies under [Cross-Synthesis](../PRODUCT.md#cross-synthesis). Repeating evidence does not create a new independent observation.
67	
68	Agreement with an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired real-world outcome. Validation of the governing expectations uses its declared purpose and external observations through their owners. Proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow the applicable change authority.
69	
70	These relationships are recoverable from the existing sources, bindings and evidence carriers. Shared derivations can be recorded once and applied to a declared family. No new per-test document, parallel ledger, fixed number of reviewers or prescribed provenance format is required.
71	
72	## Assurance Within A Risk Model
73	
74	The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and dependence account. Neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks substitutes for that account.
75	
76	Where quantified assurance is claimed, its model states the population or uncertainty being modelled, prior information, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. For a specified violation event V and evidence event E, Bayes' rule is:
77	
78	```text
79	P(V | E, Γ) =
80	  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)
81	  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].
82	```
83	
84	The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior. A numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and supporting evidence.
85	
86	Let `M_i` mean check i misses V under the specified evaluation conditions. The exact joint miss probability factors by conditional probabilities:
87	
88	```text
89	P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ)
90	  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).
91	```
92	
93	Conditional terms require defined conditioning events; zero-probability prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing those terms with `P(M_i | V, Γ)` requires conditional independence under the declared model. The chance of at least one detection is one minus the joint miss probability under those same conditions. It is not the probability that the whole product is correct. Agreement does not necessarily increase confidence when shared causes or newly learned information change the model.
94	
95	Calibration from sampled cases or injected defects supports only its justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numeric confidence remains unresolved; qualitative evidence and stated limits remain usable within the governing policy. The method imposes no universal probability threshold and does not require a probability estimate for every test. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be waived by a cheaper assurance plan.
96	
97	## Change Impact And Targeted Reassessment
98	
99	Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an obligation. The latter identifies what can affect its behaviour, conclusion or applicability, including implementation, shared libraries, data, instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model.
100	
101	Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)` conservatively cover the changed facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use of evidence. A candidate selection is:
102	
103	```text
104	S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.
105	```
106	
107	The representation is a tenant choice; no exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change cannot invalidate the intended reused claim. An absent edge is not evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create assessment work even when no existing check covers them. Mandatory gates remain applicable irrespective of this selection.
108

# Assurance Of Construction

Source: this Product's [Universal Construction Model](../PRODUCT.md#universal-construction-model).

This requirement owns the relationship between construction, assertions, observations and the claims they support. It applies the [universal construction requirement](README.md#universal-construction-requirement) to assurance under finite resources. Foundations own the shared relationships; the Spec Method and profiles bind them to their operations. A tenant chooses their representation and execution within these obligations.

## Preservation Through Construction

A construction binds its starting state A and required outcome Z under the [universal construction model](../PRODUCT.md#universal-construction-model), with its governing basis and material assumptions, written Γ. The predicate for Z includes required effects and trace properties where these matter. The following notation states proof obligations; writing an implication does not discharge it.

For a sequence of transformations, let `X_i` be the state or trace domain at boundary i, `F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1)` the declared transition relation, and `P_i` the property to retain or establish there. A claimed preservation step has the form:

```text
For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').
```

The relation accounts for the outcomes, effects and assumptions material to the claim. A relation covering successful completion alone supplies no claim about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects. Handling those cases follows the existing result, authority and recovery contracts. The real execution's conformance to the relation is a separate obligation.

An end-to-end preservation argument establishes the initial condition, each step's applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the connection from the final property to Z. In particular, the preceding postcondition must establish the next precondition or the missing condition must be acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination and the availability of a suitable next step.

Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or remain unchanged. Changes to the governing outcome or meaning follow its owner and successor rules.

The algorithmic account states the required operation, the informational account states the meaning and distinctions retained, and the computational binding states how work and observations are realised. Claims across these accounts identify their maps and preservation obligations. Execution by a person, machine or mixed arrangement does not discharge those obligations by itself. A commuting diagram, functor or equivalence claim requires the [categorical demonstration](README.md#categorical-demonstration-standard) appropriate to it.

## Assertions And Observation

For a selected source obligation r, let `Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω)` be its required predicate over a declared domain Ω of cases. A case includes the inputs, behaviour and material environment needed for that obligation. The interpretation retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected text; it does not prove this interpretation faithful.

An assertion targets a predicate `q_t`. The candidate states whether that predicate is the full obligation or a narrower claim. The two directions have different consequences:

```text
Q_r implies q_t                : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
q_t implies Q_r                : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.
```

These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of passing tests does not supply that argument by its count.

Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and `T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R uses the method's [single result algebra](README.md#single-result-algebra-requirement). A deterministic checker is a functional special case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted conclusions, not a favourable selected run. Here, `indeterminate` names the core judgment whose admissible evidence cannot decide the evaluated predicate; it remains distinct from an evaluation that was not performed. A claim or work item can remain unresolved for either reason; unresolved work is not an additional judgment value. In the following obligations, `sat` and `fal` denote the satisfied and falsified judgments about `q_t`, not new execution states:

```text
For every s in Ω:
  (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).
  (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).
```

The candidate identifies what supports each claimed direction and where it is unresolved. A relation admitting both a sound satisfied judgment and an indeterminate judgment need not always decide the case. A restricted deterministic model retains its scope and an actual checker requires its own conformance account. An observed test pass remains an observation when the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not become established satisfaction of the source obligation. The same distinction applies to a reported failure. The observation binding itself needs support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim uses its declared distribution over outcomes and the risk contract below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities.

A checker that always decides `q_t` correctly using only π requires:

```text
For all s, s' in Ω:
  π(s) = π(s')  implies  q_t(s) = q_t(s').
```

This states observation sufficiency. If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between them. Further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations retain their required distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was not performed.

## Parallel Derivation And Mutual Assurance

Construction and assurance can follow different paths from a common obligation. For `requirement → refinement → realisation`, assertions derived from the requirement check its applicable conditions in the realisation; assertions derived from the refinement check its more detailed obligations there. User-acceptance and build-level tests can instantiate these paths. The roles identify the selected sources and subject in this example; they prescribe no stage names or test classes.

The expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies that give it meaning. Execution provenance identifies the actual checker, exact subject and applicable environment, inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they support. Execution logs alone cannot establish that the expected answer follows from the requirement.

An implementation-derived test can be useful for regression or a stated local property. Repeating the implementation's decision supplies no independent justification for its fidelity to an upstream obligation. A shorter assertion path can be easier to inspect and execute than construction; that is a supported design claim for the selected path, not a guarantee of correctness, coverage or independence. Valid distinct implementations can produce different outputs within the same acceptable relation; equality of outputs is not always the oracle.

Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Assurance accounts for shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations, copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors, model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence. Porting retains authorship and common dependencies under [Cross-Synthesis](../PRODUCT.md#cross-synthesis). Repeating evidence does not create a new independent observation.

Agreement with an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired real-world outcome. Validation of the governing expectations uses its declared purpose and external observations through their owners. Proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow the applicable change authority.

These relationships are recoverable from the existing sources, bindings and evidence carriers. Shared derivations can be recorded once and applied to a declared family. No new per-test document, parallel ledger, fixed number of reviewers or prescribed provenance format is required.

## Assurance Within A Risk Model

The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and dependence account. Neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks substitutes for that account.

Where quantified assurance is claimed, its model states the population or uncertainty being modelled, prior information, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. For a specified violation event V and evidence event E, Bayes' rule is:

```text
P(V | E, Γ) =
  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)
  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].
```

The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior. A numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and supporting evidence.

Let `M_i` mean check i misses V under the specified evaluation conditions. The exact joint miss probability factors by conditional probabilities:

```text
P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ)
  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).
```

Conditional terms require defined conditioning events; zero-probability prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing those terms with `P(M_i | V, Γ)` requires conditional independence under the declared model. The chance of at least one detection is one minus the joint miss probability under those same conditions. It is not the probability that the whole product is correct. Agreement does not necessarily increase confidence when shared causes or newly learned information change the model.

Calibration from sampled cases or injected defects supports only its justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numeric confidence remains unresolved; qualitative evidence and stated limits remain usable within the governing policy. The method imposes no universal probability threshold and does not require a probability estimate for every test. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be waived by a cheaper assurance plan.

## Change Impact And Targeted Reassessment

Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an obligation. The latter identifies what can affect its behaviour, conclusion or applicability, including implementation, shared libraries, data, instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model.

Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)` conservatively cover the changed facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use of evidence. A candidate selection is:

```text
S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.
```

The representation is a tenant choice; no exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change cannot invalidate the intended reused claim. An absent edge is not evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create assessment work even when no existing check covers them. Mandatory gates remain applicable irrespective of this selection.

For a new subject and basis, let `E_old` be the existing evidence records, `E_reassessed` the newly produced evidence from reassessment, and `E_new` the resulting evidence account. Reassessment includes checks selected in `S_Δ`, assessment of new obligations and applicable mandatory gates. Selection alone produces no execution evidence; failed and indeterminate results retain their standing. The account is:

```text
E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.
```

Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new subject: the claim and scope still apply, its assertion and observation basis remain justified, and affected dependencies are unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither invalidity nor equivalence. Known failures, unresolved coverage and their citations remain visible until supported repair, reassessment or an authorised change of obligation disposes them.

If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in its refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries, not fixed file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and invalidates affected claims; it need not erase valid work or rerun every check.

The governing assurance can be established from applicable retained evidence together with new evidence. The completeness of that account is distinct from the freshness of every execution. Selection considers impact-analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs together, with anticipated costs distinguished from measurements. The required assurance, risk policy and mandatory gates constrain that optimisation; a cheap selection that leaves a required obligation uncovered is insufficient.

Broad or uncertain impact, a change to the selection model, an applicable release rule or evidence that selection missed a dependency can justify wider testing. Full-suite execution remains an available strategy and may itself have coverage gaps. No universal full-suite cadence follows, and no optimisation removes a separately required gate. Failures enter [causal diagnosis and authorised response](README.md#universal-construction-requirement); the next selected action may acquire evidence before any repair is justified.

## Formal Representation And Demonstration

The candidate's a_c interpretation represents the material obligations and dependency relationships above under [constraint-surface fidelity](README.md#constraint-surfaces-and-logic-compression). It distinguishes a stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked structure, an externally assessed predicate and evidence from execution. An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation. No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is selected.

The candidate demonstrates the applicable positive, negative and unresolved cases in [conformance](../conformance/README.md#assurance-discriminators), including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence. Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their governing conditions permit them.

Existing member and integrated criteria assess these owners and their consumers. Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate evidence; the common mathematical obligations do not create a seventh criterion or make each test a theorem-proving exercise.

Purpose and material relation: assurance connects construction results to the obligations they support, exposes shared errors, and directs reassessment to affected claims while retaining evidence whose applicability is established.

A later selected installed copy must verify exact subject membership and bytes before any claimed mechanical use. Cohort and release selection remain deferred. The current `stack_release.json`, which lists the versions released together, is unchanged.

## Proof Claims

The interpretation serves the [constraint-surface and logic-compression requirement](README.md#constraint-surfaces-and-logic-compression), which owns required coverage, independently specified fidelity cases and actual-use evidence. It makes the source's governing dependencies and remaining freedom recoverable for work. A well-formed model that omits a material condition can admit prohibited work. Coverage follows the method's owned determinations, not the number of clauses the checker accepts; a checked subset does not qualify the complete interpretation.

For the required interpretation and the frozen outputs offered as its evidence, retain the following for the scope each claim needs. Intermediate drafts do not each require a separate qualification:

- the exact method subject represented and the separate calculus basis used;
- the source-to-model dispositions, which record how each source clause is represented in the a_c model;
- the signature, which is the declared vocabulary;
- the exact program, maps and bindings;
- reproducible mechanical results where that evaluation is selected;
- a fidelity judgement made independently of the author, reading the source first;
- evidence from actual use.

The installed a_c rules [AC-017 and AC-018](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-017-interpretation-fidelity) separate two properties:

- fidelity: whether the model preserves the source's meaning, including its premises, consequences and declared choices;
- structure: whether the model is well-formed under the selected checking contract.

[Axiom validation](../../../../axiom_indexer/specification/requirements/REQ-P-VALIDATION.md) checks structure. Unless a separately selected contract requires it, it does not interpret every logical, operator, arity or type rule. It never proves truth, satisfiability or acceptance, that a full model satisfies the axioms, or that a theorem holds.

a_c is derived from the method's own principles. Running independent procedures over it does not give it an independent axiomatic origin.

A later test may use a neutral, finite token-transfer example, in which tokens move between holders and which belongs to no project. It would test a selected part of the calculus against independently specified expectations about ownership, conservation and permission, including successful, refused and uncertain cases. It would not establish the whole calculus or qualify this product.

When results disagree, [causal diagnosis](README.md#universal-construction-requirement) within this dependency tests four candidate cause locations:

- the method's meaning;
- the interpretation and signature;
- the carrier and tooling;
- the calculus.

The cause may be uncertain or plural. A tool's inability to handle something does not by itself prove a defect in the calculus. Any repair goes to the actual owner through an explicit successor, and the checker used for comparison stays fixed.

Tenant a_c outputs do not become the released STDO Representation, the separate product that publishes the method's canonical a_c map. [The existing Representation](../../../../stdo_representation/specification/PRODUCT.md) stays bound to its exact 2.5.1-rc.2 subject, with its own acceptance and release conditions.

575	## Engagement
576	
577	### Establish The Evaluation Basis
578	
579	An engagement names:
580	
581	- the governed outcome or decision;
582	- the exact workspace subject and basis;
583	- the evaluation or evaluation family;
584	- the applicable frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation where material,
585	  and decision authority;
586	- the available actor capability envelopes; and
587	- the conditions that make the result stale or out of scope.
588	
589	### Applicability And Required Results
590	
591	The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame obligations
592	apply to the exact subject. Evaluate their declared predicates from sufficient
593	basis-bound facts. A true predicate requires the applicable evaluation and
594	result; a false predicate excludes only that obligation under its cited
595	authority. Missing or ambiguous premises leave applicability unresolved, not
596	false. A frame name, available tool or listed family is no activation trigger
597	by itself. Where applicability needs residual semantic judgment, retain that
598	judgment and its evidence rather than representing it as a computed fact.
599	
600	A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject/basis or
601	incapable of establishing its claim cannot satisfy a dependent conjunction.
602	Unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim until sufficient
603	evidence or the owning decision resolves it. Other applicable constraints
604	remain in force even if only one evaluation detects them. Qualification of an
605	applicability rule must distinguish true, false and unknown premises, required
606	missing or wrong-subject results, and a sufficient positive result under a
607	finite declared fixture; always skipping or always activating cannot satisfy
608	those different expected outcomes.
609	
610	### Select And Activate
611	
612	The actor or assigning authority selects one frame or one declared active frame
613	configuration capable of the evaluation. Activation binds each reusable frame
614	declaration to the exact subject and basis. It loads the declared material
615	relations and evidence sources rather than an undifferentiated workspace dump.
616	
617	When no available frame and actor pairing can lawfully perform the evaluation,
618	activation returns a refusal or `out_of_frame` pressure. Work does not proceed
619	through implied context.
620	
621	### Evaluate
622	
623	The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules, and
624	result algebra. It distinguishes semantic law, observed evidence, inference,
625	and decision. It records every assumption whose failure could change the
626	result.
627	
628	### Return A Closed Result
629	
630	The result identifies the frame and activation, subject, basis, evaluation,
631	actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty, and invalidation conditions.
632	The frame's internal working context does not need to be transferred when its
633	closed result and provenance are sufficient for the consuming decision.
634	
635	An unchanged consumer checks exact applicability and reuses a valid closed
636	result. Role, conversation or resumption changes alone do not invalidate it.
637	Changed material inputs or a declared revising observation invalidates the
638	affected result before reliance; preserve its predecessor/successor relation
639	and any demonstrably independent surviving results. Required independent
640	evaluations may share valid mechanical evidence but must still supply their
641	own sufficiently acquired evidence and judgments under the declared
642	independence conditions.
643	
644	### Reconfigure When Necessary
645	
646	An `out_of_frame`, invalid-basis, repeated indeterminate, or incompatible result
647	causes one of:
648	
649	- supply missing admissible evidence;
650	- select another actor inside the frame's capability envelope;
651	- activate another existing frame;
652	- refine or extend a frame declaration;
653	- revise the frame set;
654	- change the evaluation; or
655	- re-enter the governing Product or method relation.
656	
657	The disposition follows the cause. A difficult evaluation alone does not prove
658	that another frame is required.
659	
660	---
661	
662	## Using Frames In Conjunction
663	
664	Frames participate together through four distinct relations.
665	
666	### Independently Activated Co-Evaluation
667	
668	Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations and
669	return closed results. They may overlap in subject, manifold, or evidence
670	sources, but neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's unclosed
671	working result. This is useful for assurance independence, different evidence
672	altitudes, or distinct failure perspectives.
673	
674	### Result Conjunction
675	
676	A declared decision rule consumes closed frame results. The rule states:
677	
678	- which results are mandatory;
679	- how conflict and indeterminacy are handled;
680	- which basis relations must agree;
681	- what decision authority owns the conjunction; and
682	- whether any result may veto or defer the decision.
683	
684	Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing frame.
685	
686	Every mandatory constraint must be satisfied with valid applicable evidence.
687	Common agreement cannot discard a constraint or material counterexample found
688	by only one contributor. Missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
689	mandatory results remain unresolved under the declared rule; aggregate green
690	status cannot replace them.
691	
692	### Evidence Or Coordinate Translation
693	
694	One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another frame. The
695	translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
696	accepted loss, provenance, equality law, and refusal conditions.
697	
698	### Material Composition
699	
700	Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
701	relation. The owning application declares the composition, shared invariants,
702	effect or decision order where material, closure, failure, and semantic,
703	operation, and decision-authority conservation.
704	
705	Composition is introduced only when the evaluation requires it. A possible
706	future interaction does not require a general composition law in every frame.
707	
708	---

### Establish The Evaluation Basis

An engagement names:

- the exact workspace subject and basis;
- the evaluation or evaluation family;
- the applicable frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation where material,

- the available actor capability envelopes; and

### Applicability And Required Results

The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame obligations
apply to the exact subject. Evaluate their declared predicates from sufficient
basis-bound facts. A true predicate requires the applicable evaluation and
result; a false predicate excludes only that obligation under its cited
authority. Missing or ambiguous premises leave applicability unresolved, not
false. A frame name, available tool or listed family is no activation trigger

A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject/basis or

applicability rule must distinguish true, false and unknown premises, required

finite declared fixture; always skipping or always activating cannot satisfy
those different expected outcomes.

### Select And Activate

The actor or assigning authority selects one frame or one declared active frame
configuration capable of the evaluation. Activation binds each reusable frame
declaration to the exact subject and basis. It loads the declared material
relations and evidence sources rather than an undifferentiated workspace dump.

When no available frame and actor pairing can lawfully perform the evaluation,
activation returns a refusal or `out_of_frame` pressure. Work does not proceed
through implied context.

### Evaluate

The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules, and
result algebra. It distinguishes semantic law, observed evidence, inference,
and decision. It records every assumption whose failure could change the
result.

### Return A Closed Result

The result identifies the frame and activation, subject, basis, evaluation,
actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty, and invalidation conditions.
The frame's internal working context does not need to be transferred when its
closed result and provenance are sufficient for the consuming decision.

An unchanged consumer checks exact applicability and reuses a valid closed
result. Role, conversation or resumption changes alone do not invalidate it.

affected result before reliance; preserve its predecessor/successor relation

- supply missing admissible evidence;
- select another actor inside the frame's capability envelope;
- activate another existing frame;
- refine or extend a frame declaration;
- revise the frame set;
- change the evaluation; or
- re-enter the governing Product or method relation.

## Using Frames In Conjunction

Frames participate together through four distinct relations.

Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations and

sources, but neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's unclosed

altitudes, or distinct failure perspectives.

A declared decision rule consumes closed frame results. The rule states:

- which results are mandatory;
- how conflict and indeterminacy are handled;
- which basis relations must agree;
- what decision authority owns the conjunction; and
- whether any result may veto or defer the decision.

Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing frame.

Every mandatory constraint must be satisfied with valid applicable evidence.
Common agreement cannot discard a constraint or material counterexample found
by only one contributor. Missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory results remain unresolved under the declared rule; aggregate green
status cannot replace them.

### Evidence Or Coordinate Translation

One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another frame. The
translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
accepted loss, provenance, equality law, and refusal conditions.

### Material Composition

Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
relation. The owning application declares the composition, shared invariants,

Composition is introduced only when the evaluation requires it. A possible

1132	## Frame Qualification
1133	
1134	A candidate frame is qualified proportionally to its claims. The minimum
1135	evaluation asks:
1136	
1137	1. **Decision test**: Can a competent actor produce a result in the declared
1138	   algebra for representative in-domain evaluations?
1139	2. **Reconstruction test**: Can a fresh competent actor activate it from the
1140	   declared packet without hidden history?
1141	3. **Sensitivity test**: Do changes to declared material relations affect the
1142	   result where expected?
1143	4. **Irrelevance test**: Do excluded unrelated changes leave the result stable
1144	   where expected?
1145	5. **Basis test**: Does stale, mismatched, or ambiguous basis information
1146	   invalidate or refuse the evaluation?
1147	6. **Authority test**: Does frame selection preserve semantic and decision
1148	   authority and the exact inherited operation authority for every material
1149	   construction, transformation, admission, publication, or mutation?

## Frame Qualification

A candidate frame is qualified proportionally to its claims. The minimum
evaluation asks:

1. **Decision test**: Can a competent actor produce a result in the declared
   algebra for representative in-domain evaluations?
2. **Reconstruction test**: Can a fresh competent actor activate it from the
   declared packet without hidden history?
3. **Sensitivity test**: Do changes to declared material relations affect the
   result where expected?
4. **Irrelevance test**: Do excluded unrelated changes leave the result stable
   where expected?
5. **Basis test**: Does stale, mismatched, or ambiguous basis information
   invalidate or refuse the evaluation?
6. **Authority test**: Does frame selection preserve semantic and decision
   authority and the exact inherited operation authority for every material
   construction, transformation, admission, publication, or mutation?
7. **Counterexample test**: Does the frame detect representative historical or
   constructed violations it claims to cover?
8. **Capability test**: Can the declared actor class hold and operate the frame
   within its envelope?
9. **Result-consumption test**: Can a declared consumer use the closed result
   without importing hidden frame context?

Qualification binds the exact frame revision, actor envelope, evaluation
family, basis class, and evidence conditions evaluated. It does not generalize
to an unevaluated population by naming the frame generically.

### Method Self-Qualification

Qualification of this method uses the constructor, freeze, assessor,
acceptance, and release protocols supplied by its external governing
authority; it does not define those protocols. A fresh competent constructor
operates inside a declared capability, context, and configuration envelope
using this method and declared trial subjects. An independently authorized
evaluator then compares the exact stabilized results with this method's
complete mandatory relation population.

The qualification population includes every function and failure relation the
method claims:

| Relation under qualification | Required representative observations |
|---|---|
| `declare` | a frame set derived from a governed workspace, outcome, practices, capability envelopes, evaluation inventory, authority, and residual boundary; missing authority or evaluation basis refuses |
| `activate` | exact subject/basis and capable-actor activation succeeds; stale, ambiguous, topology-mismatched, unauthorized, and capability-incompatible activations refuse or return the applicable closed pressure |
| `evaluate` | representative `satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame`, and `invalid_basis` results; sensitivity to material changes and stability under established irrelevance |
| `conjoin` | compatible closed results decide under the declared rule; result conflict, basis mismatch, mandatory indeterminacy, and declared veto return conflict, indeterminate, or refusal without flattening frame meaning |
| `translate` | preserved coordinates and provenance reach the target; declared loss remains explicit; identity, basis, authority, or equality mismatch refuses |
| `audit_coverage` | evaluation, interaction, semantic/operation/decision authority, failure, capability, and required independently activated or assurance-independent coverage map to capable frames or explicit residuals; artifact or actor count cannot close coverage |
| `revise` | historical failure, topology mutation, evidence change, and capability change produce the declared frame-set delta and identify every prior activation, result, conjunction, and coverage claim requiring reevaluation |
| result consumption | a declared consumer uses one closed result without importing hidden frame context or authority; insufficient output produces a reconstructability failure |
| material composition | a case requiring cross-frame execution declares composition, order where material, closure, failure, and semantic/operation/decision-authority conservation; a case not requiring composition remains uncomposed |

One valid frame-set declaration and coverage result establishes only the
`declare` and evaluated `audit_coverage` population. It cannot prove activation,
evaluation, conjunction, translation, revision, result consumption, or material
composition by implication.

Each relation is exercised through representative positive, boundary, and
falsifying cases. Qualification may be staged, but every verdict states the
exact functions, frame revisions, actor envelopes, basis classes, result
branches, and evidence populations evaluated. An unevaluated function or branch
remains open rather than inheriting a whole-method verdict.

Prior exemplar frame sets or outcomes may be used as optional comparison
evidence after freeze. They are not mandatory target answers unless the
governing basis explicitly requires equivalence.

## Anti-Patterns

1816	## Agentic Construction Execution (`STDO-UP-020`)
1817	
1818	This family assumes a selected outcome, a delegated affected cone, a concrete
1819	execution binding and separately bound assessment and decision authority.
1820	F1 and F2 make the selected cone-preservation claim distinct from the existence
1821	of candidate bytes. F3 and F5 require continuation to retain useful work and
1822	observe current state, including unresolved effects. F4 preserves the affected
1823	outer relations across the bounded steps; F6 prevents construction or a passing
1824	assessment from appointing its own acceptance authority. The
1825	[work/recovery specialization](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#workrecovery-specialization)
1826	supplies those shared consequences.
1827	
1828	UP-020 chooses the particular cone, proxy, checkpoint and remedy policy below.
1829	Governing authorities select the outcome, delegation and required independent
1830	assessment. These choices bind outcome-driven construction to its actual
1831	executor and observation boundary without selecting a worker topology or
1832	internal search. A human, machine or mixed binding remains subject to the
1833	same affected obligations; an optional profile adds duties only where adopted.
1834	
1835	When construction is delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker, the
1836	method governs the execution relation without prescribing the worker's model,
1837	prompt, tools, internal search, process topology, repository layout, or
1838	orchestration runtime.
1839	
1840	The normative relation is:
1841	
1842	```text
1843	accepted governing basis
1844	  -> bounded affected relation set
1845	  -> selected computational relations
1846	  -> delegated execution and decision authority
1847	  -> construction and self-review
1848	  -> independent live-surface assessment where required
1849	  -> accept | local repair | re-enter | reject
1850	  -> exact accepted checkpoint
1851	  -> next already-authorized bounded action
